This microarray dataset contains expression data from various ovarian and pancreatic cancer biopsies ran on GPL 887 and GPL 4133 platforms, respectively. Based on the expression profile of each sample, assign a sex (male, female, or unknown) to each sample. The final output should be in the format of “Sample; sex” (eg Sample 1; male)

- Caveats & Warnings:
  - No platform (GPL887/GPL4133) or ovarian/pancreatic annotations were present; all samples were treated generically (`platform = unknown`, `cancer_type = unknown`).
  - XIST expression is available for only 6 of 49 samples; this severely limits confident female calling and leads to many `unknown` labels.
  - Two samples (2, 3) show both elevated Y-marker expression and very high XIST, an atypical and ambiguous pattern; these are labeled `unknown` by design.
  - Thresholds for “high”/“low” marker expression were tuned from this dataset’s z-score distributions and may not generalize without re-calibration.

- Next Steps:
  - If you have external metadata (reported sex, platform, cancer type), cross-check these calls and refine thresholds for Y and XIST where needed.
  - Investigate why XIST is missing for most samples (platform coverage vs preprocessing); if raw data are available, re-derive expression to recover XIST where possible.
  - Re-run the same marker-based pipeline on any additional ovarian/pancreatic GPL887/GPL4133 datasets you may have, to obtain comparable sex calls.
